explain.say: Now look at the puzzle piece. 60 is a brilliant sharing number. You can split it into 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20 or 30 equal parts. 100 can't even be split into 3 equal whole parts! So half an hour is 30 minutes and a quarter is 15.

explain.say: Look at the board: 6 groups of 10 minutes make 60 minutes, one whole hour. Well done! Here's a wow: a circle has 360 degrees, which is six sixties. So every clock face hides a Babylonian number trick that is about 4,000 years old!

faq.a: The Sumerians and Babylonians of ancient Mesopotamia, in modern Iraq, about 4,000 years ago or more.

faq.q: Why is 60 a good number for time?
faq.a: 60 can be shared equally in many ways: by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20 and 30. That makes halves, thirds and quarters of an hour easy.
asks: Why not 100 minutes in an hour?

faq.q: Where does the word second come from?
faq.a: It comes from the Latin for the second small part. An hour was split into 60 small parts, minutes, and each minute was split again into 60 second parts.
asks: Why is it called a second?

faq.q: When did clocks get minute hands?
faq.a: Minute hands became common in the late 1600s, after the pendulum clock made clocks accurate enough to need them.
asks: Did old clocks have minute hands?

faq.a: Yes. In the 1790s France tried 10-hour days with 100-minute hours, but people found it confusing and it was soon dropped.

facts: Babylonian astronomers used a base-60 number system that still shapes our minutes, seconds and degrees.

quiz.say: Which of these numbers divides 60 exactly?
quiz.show: Which of these numbers divides 60 exactly?
quiz.why: 12 times 5 is 60, so 12 divides it exactly.

wrong.0: 60 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 4.
wrong.2: 60 divided by 9 leaves a remainder of 6.

quiz.say: Which ancient people first counted in sixties?
quiz.show: Which ancient people first counted in sixties?
quiz.why: The Sumerians and Babylonians of Mesopotamia used base 60.

wrong.1: The Vikings lived much later and did not invent base 60.
wrong.2: The Aztecs counted in twenties, not sixties.
